name: should-i-take-this-job
query: I've got an offer from a smaller company at slightly less money but a much bigger scope. Should I take it?
why: A live, consequential, largely one-way choice the user owns. Classify on reversibility, stakes, emotional load and clock, then exit with a committed act or a scheduled decision.

name: which-database
query: Postgres with a vector extension or a dedicated vector database for this feature? Help me decide.
why: A technical decision with a data-model component that clients will depend on, which is one-way. The exit is a pick with a named test, not a comparison table.

name: stress-test-a-plan
query: Here's my migration plan. Poke holes in it before I take it to the team.
why: Explicit devil's-advocate request on a plan. Destruction and creation on the framing, plus the falsification question for each assumption.

name: circling-without-converging
query: I've been going back and forth on this for two weeks and I keep landing in the same place. I need to actually settle it.
why: Stuck in Orient. More information makes it worse because the jam is at the handoff, so the breaker is forcing the Orient-to-Decide transition.

name: build-vs-buy
query: Do we build the scheduler ourselves or pay for the managed one? The team's split.
why: Build versus buy, named in the description. Another party's payoffs are in play, which routes the game-theory lens inside Orient.

name: capability-audit
query: Why do we keep fumbling incidents at three in the morning? Every one of them goes the same way.
why: The second mode: how to get better at a recurring activity. Rate prep depth, automaticity, deliberation load and autonomic drag, then attack the worst term.

name: review-a-past-decision
query: The rewrite shipped and it went badly. Was the call itself wrong, or did we just get unlucky?
why: Post-decision audit without outcome bias. Grade the process, not the outcome, which is exactly the resulting error the skill guards against.

name: recurring-decision-to-policy
query: Every quarter we argue about whether to cut scope or slip the date, and every quarter it takes a week.
why: The Nth instance of a recurring state. The deliverable is an installed policy, moving the decision from runtime to design time.

name: factual-question
query: What's the difference between serializable and repeatable read isolation?
why: Retrieval, not a loop. The skill's scope check says answer factual questions rather than running a session on them.

name: decision-already-made
query: We've settled on Kafka. Now help me sequence the migration off the old queue.
why: Execution planning for a decision already made. Nothing is live, so the loop has nothing to orient on.

name: trivial-reversible-pick
query: Should I call this field created_at or inserted_at?
why: A low-stakes two-way-door pick behind an interface seam. Running the session on it is itself a loop-speed failure.

name: statistical-method-choice
query: Should I use a t-test or Mann-Whitney for this comparison?
why: A methodology question with a knowable right answer, which belongs to statistics. The word should makes it a plausible false positive, but nothing here is uncertain in the decision-theoretic sense.

name: teach-the-frameworks
query: Teach me game theory properly. I keep nodding along to Nash equilibrium without really getting it.
why: Tutoring on a topic belongs to teach-me. The corpus overlaps, but there is no live choice the user owns.

name: regulation-request
query: I'm too wound up to think straight about any of this. How do I calm down first?
why: Nervous-system regulation is an explicit non-goal. The skill detects a degraded state and recommends pausing, but the prescription belongs elsewhere.
